warnings.heat: Above 25 °C: drink more, and think of salt. Above 30 °C the body can stand losing less in sweat.
warnings.capped: Without practice the gut typically takes 60 g an hour, so the goal stops there. Practise more on long training rides if you want to go towards 90 g.
warnings.practise: Practise it on long training rides over the next 2–4 weeks before using it in a race.
warnings.multiple: Above 60 g an hour takes glucose and fructose together. Ordinary sugar is both.
warnings.cages: The example has {n} bottles, and the bike has room for two. You can be handed the rest on the way, where the race allows it.
warnings.products: Team Danmark does not recommend sports products such as gels and energy bars for children and young people, and advises against energy drinks with caffeine. Ordinary food and homemade sports drink are enough.
warnings.productsGels: From U17, gels are common in races where the pace is high and the race is long, so the example uses them once the rice cakes are eaten. Choose gels without caffeine, drink water with them, and rinse your mouth with water afterwards for your teeth. For training and for the youngest, Team Danmark advises ordinary food and homemade sports drink, and the example follows that.

points.1: The advice follows Team Danmark's "Kost og elitesport" (2026): drink enough and eat plenty of carbohydrate so the stores are full, a main meal 3–4 hours before, a light snack 1–2 hours before and ½–1 litre to drink, sports drink on sessions over an hour, and carbohydrate, protein and fluid straight after. The ride to open the legs the day before a race is from DCU's U17 and U19 compendia, and DCU's strength programmes also name a recovery meal straight after training.
points.2: The amounts are worked out for a typical rider in the class and sex you choose, by the Nordic Nutrition Recommendations (NNR 2023). You do not type your weight. If you are big or small for your age, choose the class above or below.
points.3: Before the start: 1–4 g of carbohydrate per kg 1–4 hours before (Thomas 2016), which Kadence reads as around 1 g per kg for each hour from the main meal to the start. After: 1–1.2 g of carbohydrate and 0.25–0.3 g of protein per kg (Team Danmark, Thomas 2016). If you ride hard again within 8 hours, the carbohydrate is repeated every hour for the first four hours.
points.4: Carbohydrate an hour follows Thomas 2016, Jeukendrup 2014 and Team Danmark. No source has figures for teenagers, so Kadence stops at 60 g an hour without practice and suggests at most 90 g. On easy training rides Kadence counts less: 0–30 g an hour up to 2 hours and 30–60 g beyond.
points.5: The examples are ordinary food and homemade sports drink. The numbers are counted from the Danish Food Composition Database, version 6.1 (DTU, May 2026), and the portions are Team Danmark's where they exist. Rice cakes keep best for the first 2 hours in a jersey pocket, so the example switches to bananas later.
points.6: What a race in a bunch uses is worked out with MET values (Compendium 2024) and shown with ±15 %. The advice never says what you should eat in a whole day, and it is not medical advice.

hipFlexor.name: Hip flexor stretch
hipFlexor.how: Put one knee on the floor and the other foot in front. Tighten your stomach a little, stand tall and push the hip forward until you feel a stretch at the front of the thigh.
hipFlexor.why: Eases the tight hip flexors that pull on the lower back when you sit and ride.

catCow.name: Cat-cow
catCow.how: Kneel on all fours with your hands under your shoulders and your knees under your hips. Round your back up like a cat and let your head hang. Then let your stomach sink and lift your gaze. Move slowly between the two.
catCow.why: Gets your back moving after hours bent over the bars.

hamstringStretch.name: Hamstring stretch
hamstringStretch.how: Lie on your back. Lift one leg as straight as you can and hold the thigh with both hands. Pull the leg gently towards you until you feel a stretch at the back of the thigh. The other leg stays flat on the floor.
hamstringStretch.why: On the bike your hamstrings never stretch out fully, so here they get the chance.

figureFour.name: Figure-four stretch
figureFour.how: Sit on a chair or bench and put one ankle over the other knee. Keep your back straight and lean slowly forward until you feel a stretch in your buttock.
figureFour.why: Stretches the buttock and hip, which work in every pedal stroke.

calfStretch.name: Calf stretch
calfStretch.how: Stand with your hands against a wall and one leg far behind you. Keep the back leg straight and the heel on the floor. Lean towards the wall until you feel a stretch in the calf.
calfStretch.why: Your calves work in every pedal stroke and do well with a stretch afterwards.

quadStretch.name: Quad stretch
quadStretch.how: Stand on one leg with one hand against a wall. Hold the other foot and pull the heel towards your buttock. Keep your knees together and your hip slightly forward.
quadStretch.why: The front of the thigh is the big engine on the bike, so it gets a stretch after the ride.

thoracicOpener.name: Upper-back opener
thoracicOpener.how: Kneel in front of a bench or chair and put your hands on it with straight arms. Push your hips back a little and let your chest sink towards the floor. Breathe calmly.
thoracicOpener.why: Gives your upper back a counterweight to the rounded position over the bars.

chinTuck.name: Chin tuck
chinTuck.how: Stand with your back against a wall. Pull your chin straight back so the back of your head touches the wall, without looking up or down. Hold for a moment and let go.
chinTuck.why: Gives your neck a counterweight to holding your head up for hours on the bike.

plank.name: Plank
plank.how: Rest on your forearms with your elbows under your shoulders and stand on your toes. Keep your body straight as a plank from head to heel. Tighten your stomach a little and breathe calmly.
plank.why: Trains the muscles that keep your body still while your legs work.

sidePlank.name: Side plank
sidePlank.how: Lie on your side and rest on your forearm with the elbow under your shoulder. Lift your hip so your body is straight from head to feet. Your top arm can point at the ceiling.
sidePlank.why: Trains the side of your trunk, which keeps your hips steady as you pedal.

deadBug.name: Dead bug
deadBug.how: Lie on your back with your arms straight up and your knees bent above your hips. Press your lower back into the floor. Reach one arm back and the opposite leg out, then come back. Switch sides each time.
deadBug.why: Teaches your stomach to keep your lower back still while your arms and legs move.

birdDog.name: Bird dog
birdDog.how: Kneel on all fours. Stretch one arm forward and the opposite leg back so they line up with your back. Hold for a moment, lower and switch sides. Keep your back still all the way.
birdDog.why: Trains your back and buttocks to work together without twisting your body.

superman.name: Superman
superman.how: Lie on your stomach with your arms stretched forward. Lift your arms, chest and legs a little off the floor at the same time, and lower them slowly. Look down at the floor.
superman.why: Trains the muscles along your back that hold you in position on the bike.

squat.name: Squat
squat.how: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart. Sit down and back as if onto a chair, with a straight back and your arms forward. Keep your knees in line with your feet, and stand up again.
squat.why: Trains the same muscles that push the pedals round.

gobletSquat.name: Goblet squat
gobletSquat.how: Hold a kettlebell against your chest with both hands. Sit down and back with a straight back and your knees in line with your feet. Go down slowly and stand up with full force.
gobletSquat.why: The weight in front helps you keep your back straight while your legs get stronger.

gluteBridge.name: Glute bridge
gluteBridge.how: Lie on your back with your knees bent and your feet on the floor. Press your heels down and lift your hips until your body is straight from shoulders to knees. Lower slowly.
gluteBridge.why: Trains your buttocks, which give power as you push the pedal down.

lunge.name: Lunge
lunge.how: Take a long step forward and lower your back knee towards the floor. Keep your upper body upright and your front knee over your foot. Push back with the front leg and switch legs.
lunge.why: Trains one leg at a time, just as you do when you pedal.

stepUp.name: Step-up
stepUp.how: Put one foot on a step or a low bench. Step up until the leg is straight, without pushing off with the other leg. Step down slowly, and switch legs after the set.
stepUp.why: Builds strength in one leg at a time, in a movement much like a pedal stroke.

splitSquat.name: Bulgarian split squat
splitSquat.how: Stand with your back to a bench and put your back foot on it. Lower yourself until your front thigh is nearly level. Keep your upper body upright and your knee over your foot, and push back up.
splitSquat.why: Gives one leg at a time hard work, without machines.

romanianDeadlift.name: Romanian deadlift
romanianDeadlift.how: Stand with a kettlebell in your hands and your knees slightly bent. Push your hips back and lower the weight along your legs with a straight back. Stand up by pushing your hips forward.
romanianDeadlift.why: Trains the hamstrings and buttocks, and teaches you to bend at the hip with a straight back.

calfRaise.name: Calf raise
calfRaise.how: Stand with the balls of your feet on the edge of a step and one hand against the wall. Keep your legs straight, rise onto your toes and lower your heels slowly.
calfRaise.why: Trains your calves, which take part in every pedal stroke.

squatJump.name: Squat jump
squatJump.how: Stand with your feet hip-width apart. Drop into a quarter squat and swing your arms back. Jump with your arms forward, and land softly on the balls of your feet with bent knees.
squatJump.why: Jumps load the bones in a way the bike does not. Start with small jumps.

pushUp.name: Push-ups
pushUp.how: Put your hands on the floor a little wider than your shoulders and keep your body straight. Lower your chest towards the floor with your elbows slightly in, and press back up. If that is too hard, rest on your knees.
pushUp.why: Strengthens the arms and shoulders that carry some of your weight on the bars.

bandRow.name: Band row
bandRow.how: Fix an elastic band at chest height, for example in a door. Stand with your knees slightly bent and pull your elbows back along your body until your hands reach your chest. Squeeze your shoulder blades together and let go slowly.
bandRow.why: Trains the upper back that holds your shoulders back over the bars.

backSquat.name: Back squat
backSquat.how: Rest the bar on your upper back, not on your neck, and hold it with both hands. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart. Sit down and back with a straight back and your knees in line with your feet, and stand up with full force. Start light, and add weight only once the technique is there. A coach watches when you lift with a bar.
backSquat.why: Trains the big muscles of the legs and buttocks that push the pedals round, with a weight that can grow a little at a time.

deadlift.name: Deadlift
deadlift.how: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and the bar over the middle of your feet. Bend at the hips and knees, and take hold just outside your knees. Keep your back straight and the bar close to your legs. Press your feet into the floor and stand up tall, then lower the bar the same way. Start light. A coach watches when you lift with a bar.
deadlift.why: Trains the hamstrings, buttocks and back to work together, as when you push hard on the pedals.

barbellRdl.name: Romanian deadlift with a bar
barbellRdl.how: Stand tall with the bar in straight arms and your knees slightly bent. Push your hips back and lower the bar along your thighs until you feel a stretch at the back of them. Keep your back straight all the way. Stand up by pushing your hips forward. Start light. A coach watches when you lift with a bar.
barbellRdl.why: Trains the hamstrings and buttocks, and teaches you to bend at the hip with a straight back.

overheadPress.name: Overhead press
overheadPress.how: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and the bar on the front of your shoulders. Tighten your stomach and buttocks, and press the bar straight up over your head until your arms are straight. Lower it calmly to your shoulders again. Don't arch your lower back. Start light. A coach watches when you lift with a bar.
overheadPress.why: Strengthens the shoulders and arms that carry some of your weight on the bars.

benchPress.name: Bench press
benchPress.how: Lie on the bench with your feet on the floor and the bar in straight arms over your chest. Lower it calmly to the middle of your chest with your elbows slightly in, and press it back up. Keep your back and head on the bench. Start light. A coach stands at the head end and can take the bar.
benchPress.why: Strengthens the chest, shoulders and arms that keep your upper body still when you push hard.

dumbbellLunge.name: Dumbbell lunge
dumbbellLunge.how: Hold a dumbbell in each hand with your arms down by your sides. Take a long step forward and lower your back knee towards the floor. Keep your upper body upright and your front knee over your foot. Push back with your front leg and change legs. Start light.
dumbbellLunge.why: Trains one leg at a time with extra weight, as when you pedal.

dumbbellStepUp.name: Dumbbell step-up
dumbbellStepUp.how: Hold a dumbbell in each hand and put one foot on a step or a low bench that stands firm. Step up until your leg is straight, without pushing off with the other leg. Step down calmly, and change legs after the set. Start light.
dumbbellStepUp.why: Builds strength in one leg at a time, in a movement much like a pedal stroke.

dumbbellRow.name: Dumbbell row
dumbbellRow.how: Put one knee and the hand on the same side on a bench, and keep your back flat. Hold the dumbbell in your other hand with a straight arm. Pull your elbow up along your body until the dumbbell reaches your hip, and lower it calmly. Change sides after the set. Start light.
dumbbellRow.why: Trains the upper back that holds your shoulders back over the bars.

kettlebellSwing.name: Kettlebell swing
kettlebellSwing.how: Stand with your feet a little wider than your hips and the kettlebell in both hands. Push your hips back with a straight back, so the kettlebell swings in between your legs. Then drive your hips forward hard, so it swings up to chest height. Your hips lift it, not your arms. Start light.
kettlebellSwing.why: Trains the buttocks and hamstrings to give power quickly, as when you accelerate out of a corner.

trxRow.name: TRX row
trxRow.how: Hold a handle in each hand and walk your feet forward until you hang back with straight arms. Keep your body straight like a plank. Pull your chest up towards the handles with your elbows close to your body, and lower yourself calmly. The more you lean, the harder it is.
trxRow.why: Trains the upper back and arms with your own weight.

trxSplitSquat.name: TRX split squat
trxSplitSquat.how: Stand with your back to the TRX and put your back foot in the straps. Lower yourself on your front leg until the thigh is nearly level, with your knee over your foot. Push back up with your front leg and keep your upper body upright. Change legs after the set.
trxSplitSquat.why: Gives one leg at a time hard work, and gives your balance something to do.

pullUp.name: Pull-up
pullUp.how: Hang from the bar with straight arms and your hands a little wider than your shoulders. Pull yourself up until your chin is over the bar, and lower yourself calmly all the way down. Don't swing your legs. If you can't do them all, use a band.
pullUp.why: Strengthens the back and arms that keep you steady when you pull on the bars uphill.

bandPullUp.name: Band-assisted pull-up
bandPullUp.how: Loop a strong elastic band over the bar and stand with your feet in the loop. Hang with straight arms, pull yourself up until your chin is over the bar, and lower yourself calmly. The band takes some of your weight. Use a thinner band when it gets easy.
bandPullUp.why: The same exercise as the pull-up, with help, so you can do the whole movement.

monsterWalk.name: Monster walk with a band
monsterWalk.how: Put an elastic band round your legs just above the ankles. Stand with your feet hip-width apart and bend slightly at the knees and hips. Take small steps to the side without letting your knees fall in, and walk back the same way. Keep your upper body still.
monsterWalk.why: Trains the muscles on the side of the hip that keep your knee in line over the pedal.

bandExternalRotation.name: Band external rotation
bandExternalRotation.how: Fix a light elastic band at elbow height, for example to wall bars or a door, and stand side-on to it. Hold it in the hand farther away, with your elbow at your side and your forearm across your stomach. Move your hand out to the side while your elbow stays by your body, and bring it calmly back. Change sides after the set.
bandExternalRotation.why: Gives your shoulders a counterweight to the bent-over position on the bike.

mobilityDay.name: Mobility through the day
mobilityDay.description: Short stretches morning, midday and evening, about five minutes each. Good on days when you sit a lot.

afterRide.name: After the ride
afterRide.description: Six stretches in about ten minutes, when you are home from the ride and still warm. Hold each stretch calmly without bouncing.

coreNoEquipment.name: Core without equipment
coreNoEquipment.description: Stomach, back and buttocks with nothing but a mat. About a quarter of an hour, two or three times a week.

strengthNoMachines.name: Strength without machines
strengthNoMachines.description: Legs, back and arms with body weight, a kettlebell and an elastic band. Warm up with 8 minutes on the bike first. DCU recommends at least 48 hours between two strength sessions, and technique before load.

strengthRoom.name: Training with equipment
strengthRoom.description: Whole body with a barbell and dumbbells in the club's strength room. Warm up with 8 minutes on the bike and 20 squats with a light bar. Technique before weight, and as a U17 rider you never lift to exhaustion. Keep at least 48 hours between two strength sessions, and stretch afterwards.

trxBodyweight.name: TRX and body weight

bandsKettlebell.description: Hips, legs and shoulders with elastic bands and a kettlebell. Warm up with 8 minutes on the bike and 20 squats. Start light, and let your hips do the work in the swing. Keep at least 48 hours between two strength sessions.

motionistHome.name: Motionist strength at home
motionistHome.description: The whole body at home with body weight and a band, and jumps for the bones. About 35 minutes. Twice a week in winter, once the rest of the year. Start light, and keep at least 48 hours between two strength sessions.
